# Expo and React Native (iOS, Android)

These rules add to the core build skills of Shipwright.

## Rules

- Stay on a supported Expo SDK and run `npx expo-doctor` before each release: it flags incompatible native packages.
- Session tokens in expo-secure-store (Keychain and Keystore), never in AsyncStorage.
- EXPO_PUBLIC_* variables are visible in the shipped app. No secret key; calls that need one go through the server.
- Give a testID to every element a key task touches; Maestro flows and screen readers use it.
- Safe areas with react-native-safe-area-context; keyboard handled (KeyboardAvoidingView or react-native-keyboard-controller) on every input screen.
- Long lists with FlashList or FlatList (never ScrollView + map); images with expo-image, sized.
- iOS privacy manifest declared in app.json (expo.ios.privacyManifests); precise permission texts in app.json.
- Links into the app: universal links and App Links over https (expo-linking), no custom scheme for authentication.
- EAS Update: fixes and content only, pinned runtime version, staged rollout and tested rollback.
- Android builds and tests on any machine; iOS needs a Mac or an EAS cloud build (limited free tier).

## Check commands

Used by `/sw:audit`. `{pm}` is the project's package manager, `{url}` the app URL, `{host}` its host name.

| Check | Command | Passes if |
| --- | --- | --- |
| typecheck | `{pm} exec tsc --noEmit` | exit code 0 |
| lint | `npx expo lint` | exit code 0, no errors |
| test_run | `{pm} test` | exit code 0 |
| deps_audit | `{pm} audit --audit-level=high` | no high or critical advisory; then `npx expo-doctor` reports no issue |
| license_check | `npx --yes license-checker-rseidelsohn --summary --failOn 'GPL;AGPL'` | exit code 0 |
